Happy Tyrsday, folks! I wanted to share how my group's been doing initiative recently (actually, I think we started back in January, so I guess we've been using this for 7 months now).

Rolling initiative for each combat was getting tedious, and with our large (7 players, 1 DM) group it ate up more time that I would have liked it to. So, we have been rolling initiative just once a session, at the beginning, and cycling through that. We don't "reset" with each new encounter, we just pick up where we'd left off last time.

For example, Glarnack the barbarian's initiative for the session is a 16 and Flint Fireforge's initiative is a 15. Glarnack finished up an encounter by slaying the final orc. In the next room, the party is confronted with a group of zombies, and Flint will go first to open combat with them.

We've found that it really helps speed things up, since we can just jump straight into a combat ("Flint! You're up!" versus "Okay guys, roll initiative... [five minutes later] ... Alright, Jor-El goes first!").

On reddit a "Self Post" currently does not award you anything in the form of karma, which I never really understood. I was wondering if Voat would consider being a little different. Instead of giving nothing in the form of any points have a "self Post" award CCP instead of SCP or no points at all.

This would encourage self posts a little more and differentiate a self post from a "link" submission, and though technically not a "comment", a good self post, to me, can be a more interesting and provocative contribution than a linked story. I never understood why reddit had self posts not award any karma. I thought this idea might be a way to give a reward to original content and research that many people do themselves.

I am definitely interested in what people think about this.
Should/Could "Self Post" submissions on Voat award CCP instead of nothing or SCP?

It used to be that reddit gave you karma for your self posts, but people began to abuse the system, making very low effort self posts, like "Who likes ice cream?", and getting tons of karma for it.

As for changing it here, I actually think the it would be detrimental to voat's system to give CCP for self posts. Since voat does put some weight into CCP (daily number of upvoats and requiring 100 CCP for downvoating), anything that can quickly inflate that number should be avoided, in the same way that comment upvoat requests are frowned upon.

A lot of smaller subs are largely driven by self-posts, so I definitely think it makes sense to be awarded something for it. If the concern is with protecting the downvoat system, CCP for self-posts could start to apply after the 100 CCP downvoat minimum is reached.
I hope that they keep awarding SCP. Selfposts are probably the most original content we can have.

I was wondering if it could be a moderator or an individual subverse option. That way the people who spend most of their time posting in smaller subs or subs that tend to value and create self posts more can have their content contributors get awarded the more coveted CCP to allow them to fully participate in the community.

I think both text and link submissions should award Submission Contribution Points. I've seen too many posts on Reddit that should have been text posts, but someone overlayed the text on an image or included a link just to get link karma. If text submissions equal link submissions, this is less of an issue.

Let's say someone posts something completely off topic for that subverse, but it's getting a lot of upvoats from v/all, so the mods don't want to delete it. The could tag it as off topic, and it'll remain hidden when you visit that sub, but at the top, above the list of posts, have something that says [14 posts marked as Off-Topic hidden]. If the visitor wants to view the off topic discussions, they can click there and it'll show them in the list of posts.

I was wondering if anyone had any good methods of cleaning the threads on a regulated mod. The threads on my istick 50w have gotten dirty, and I've noticed that there is dirt and grime in the threads of my tanks and attys when I take them off my mod. My istick 50w has been free of all the malfunctions they are notorious for thus far, and I would like to keep it that way. I was thinking perhaps a q-tip with some rubbing alcohol or something, but im not sure.

Depending on your level of grime-atude, the first step on my mehtod is optional:

1) Get some Noxon on a Q-tip and use it on the theads (usually only necessary on brass or copper mech mods)

2) Use isopropyl alocohol to get rid of the excess Noxon

3) Allow it to air dry.

I almost exclusively use Noxon for mech mods and body threads, but if your threads are corroded, that's the way to go.
I don't think the threads are corroded, just dirty. So are you saying i could just skip the noxon and just use isopropyl alcohol on a q-tip?
That should be fine! Be careful because sometimes the cotton fibers like to stay in the 510.
I use a napkin with some isopropyl. If you use a q tip, fibers will get stuck in the threads and contribute to future grime,
personally I prefer q tips to napkins, easier to get all the way in the 510
